chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi'a, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is one of the oppressive characteristics when one who is riding forcefully takes the right of way of pedestrians.

key_terms.الرَّاكِبِ: The rider (one on a mount or vehicle).
key_terms.الطَّرِيقَ: The way/path; here implying the right of way.
key_terms.الْجُورِ: Oppression or injustice; specifically here, unfairness in rights or treatment.

ai.seo_question: What is considered an act of oppression (jaur) in daily social interactions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes this specific social slight under *al-Jaur* (oppression/injustice), illustrating how minor breaches of etiquette constitute a violation of rights (*huquq*). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a tangible component of justice, where the stronger party (the rider) must yield to the weaker (the pedestrian) to maintain social equity.
